turns.teacher: Hi Mahi! Today we’ll find directions using a magnet, like finding our way to an animal park. If a magnet hangs freely from a thread, which directions will its ends point when it stops?

ask.text: A bar magnet hangs freely from a thread. When it stops moving, in which directions do its ends point?

screen.ask: A bar magnet hangs freely from a thread. When it stops moving, in which directions do its ends point?

child.say: North aur south... I think? Haan, north-south hota hai.
child.private: Yeh toh easy hai, magnet north-south point karta hai, maine suna tha.
child.sent: North aur south... I think? Haan, north-south hota hai.

turns.teacher: Yes, tum got north and south right. Suppose the hanging magnet is turned to point east and west, then let go. What will it do when it settles?

ask.text: Predict: you hang a bar magnet from a thread, gently turn it to point east-west, and let go. What will happen?

screen.ask: Predict: you hang a bar magnet from a thread, gently turn it to point east-west, and let go. What will happen?

child.say: Uh, wapas ghoomega... north-south line mein aa jaayega. Easy hai.
child.private: Knows it goes back north-south from the first part but only half sure; bored already
child.sent: Uh, wapas ghoomega... north-south line mein aa jaayega. Easy hai.

turns.teacher: Yes, tum are right: it turns back and settles north to south. Now try a trickier one. If its north end is turned to face west and then released, where will that end point after it settles?

ask.text: For a science display, Meera suspends a magnet freely, then turns it so its N pole faces west. After she lets go and it settles, which direction will the N pole face?

screen.ask: For a science display, Meera suspends a magnet freely, then turns it so its N pole faces west. After she lets go and it settles, which direction will the N pole face?

child.say: North... I think. Kyunki magnet north-south mein settle hota hai na?
child.private: Partially knows it returns to north-south but unsure about the reversed start position.
child.sent: North... I think. Kyunki magnet north-south mein settle hota hai na?

turns.teacher: Yes, tum are right. Its north end turns back to north. Now let’s use a compass: when its needle has settled, how will tum find east?

ask.text: Your compass needle has settled. How do you find east?

screen.ask: Your compass needle has settled. How do you find east?

child.say: Compass ki needle north dikhati hai... toh east uske right side hoga. Right?
child.private: Feeling confident because I know the needle points north and I can imagine directions. But I'm just guessing about right/left without really understanding the turning.
child.sent: Compass ki needle north dikhati hai... toh east uske right side hoga. Right?

turns.teacher: Yes, tum: once the needle’s north end settles, east is to its right. The needle does not turn just because tum turn. If tum face south while the needle points north, will east be on your left or your right?

ask.text: Draw a compass face and mark N, E, S and W. If you face north, which direction is on your right?

screen.ask: Draw a compass face and mark N, E, S and W. If you face north, which direction is on your right?

child.say: Hmm... agar main south face kar rahi hoon aur needle north hai... toh compass ghumega nahi... toh right side... west hoga shayad?
child.private: Teacher ne direction ghuma diya, ab compass wali trick kaam nahi kar rahi. Guess kar rahi hoon.
child.sent: Hmm... agar main south face kar rahi hoon aur needle north hai... toh compass ghumega nahi... toh right side... west hoga shayad?

turns.teacher: Yes, tum: when you face south, west is on your right. The needle still points north. Now face north instead: which direction is on your right?

ask.text: Draw a compass face and mark N, E, S and W. If you face north, which direction is on your right?

screen.ask: Draw a compass face and mark N, E, S and W. If you face north, which direction is on your right?

child.say: East? Kyunki north face kar rahi hoon na, toh right east hota hai. Yeh toh easy hai.
child.private: recalls the whiteboard picture showing N ↑ and right side is E →. Wants to show off that she knows.
child.sent: East? Kyunki north face kar rahi hoon na, toh right east hota hai. Yeh toh easy hai.

turns.teacher: Yes, tum said east. The needle keeps pointing north even when tum turn, but nearby steel can disturb it. A compass on a wooden table and one on a steel almirah may differ. Which reading can tum trust, and why?

ask.text: Compare a compass placed on a wooden table and one placed on top of a steel almirah. Which reading can you trust, and why?

screen.ask: Compare a compass placed on a wooden table and one placed on top of a steel almirah. Which reading can you trust, and why?

child.say: Steel almirah... wo toh magnet ko disturb karta hai na? Toh uspe wala compass galat hoga. Wooden table wala sahi hoga.
child.private: She knows steel messes with magnets but can't explain why beyond 'it disturbs'.
child.sent: Steel almirah... wo toh magnet ko disturb karta hai na? Toh uspe wala compass galat hoga. Wooden table wala sahi hoga.

turns.teacher: Yes, tum: nearby steel can disturb the needle, so trust the compass on the wooden table. Now suppose tum bring a bar magnet close to that compass. What will happen to its needle?

ask.text: Predict: you slowly bring a bar magnet close to a compass lying on the table. What happens to the needle?

screen.ask: Predict: you slowly bring a bar magnet close to a compass lying on the table. What happens to the needle?

child.say: Haan... magnet ke paas laane se needle move karega, I think... pata nahi, north-south se hatega?
child.private: Needle ghoomega, par kaise? Bar magnet ka N end compass N ko attract karega ya repel? Confusion hai.
child.sent: Haan... magnet ke paas laane se needle move karega, I think... pata nahi, north-south se hatega?

turns.teacher: Haan, tum have the idea: a nearby magnet can pull the compass needle away from north-south. Let’s make it simpler. If the magnet comes closer, will the needle stay still or turn?

ask.text: Predict: you slowly bring a bar magnet close to a compass lying on the table. What happens to the needle?

screen.ask: Predict: you slowly bring a bar magnet close to a compass lying on the table. What happens to the needle?

child.say: Turn karega... magnet ke paas aane se. Pata nahi, maybe needle magnet ki taraf point karegi?
child.private: I know magnet messes with compass... but does it point to the magnet or just shake? Not sure. Just guessing.
child.sent: Turn karega... magnet ke paas aane se. Pata nahi, maybe needle magnet ki taraf point karegi?

turns.teacher: Haan, tum: the needle will turn. Its exact position depends on which pole of the bar magnet is near it, so it may not point straight at the magnet. How could tum use a compass to find the east wall of a classroom?

ask.text: Your group must find which wall of a new classroom faces east, using a compass. What steps will you follow?

screen.ask: Your group must find which wall of a new classroom faces east, using a compass. What steps will you follow?

child.say: Pehle compass ko table pe rakhenge, phir needle settle hone tak wait karenge. Needle north dikhayegi... toh jis taraf needle ka north point kare, woh north wall hai. Phir right side dekhne pe east wall mil jaayegi. Bas itna hi hai, easy!
child.private: Feeling confident, I can just say the steps out loud instead of doing it. This is like the earlier east question.
child.sent: Pehle compass ko table pe rakhenge, phir needle settle hone tak wait karenge. Needle north dikhayegi... toh jis taraf needle ka north point kare, woh north wall hai. Phir right side dekhne pe east wall mil jaayegi. Bas itna hi hai, easy!

turns.teacher: Tum would let the needle settle and find east to the right of north. But a compass on a steel table can point the wrong way, and the north end may point toward a corner, not a wall. Where should tum place the compass before trusting its direction?

ask.text: Your group must find which wall of a new classroom faces east, using a compass. What steps will you follow?

screen.ask: Your group must find which wall of a new classroom faces east, using a compass. What steps will you follow?
screen.studio: revealed: whiteboard written board: "steel table: needle dist" "wooden table: away from" "N ↑" "E →"

child.say: Hmm... pehle hum compass ko... wooden table pe rakhenge, kyunki steel table needle ko disturb karta hai. Phir... wait karenge needle settle hone tak... needle north dikhayegi... phir right side... east wall hogi. Bas, thak gayi, aur nahi karna!
child.private: Teacher ne steel table ke baare mein hint diya, lekin main already jaanti thi. East kaise dhoondna hai, yeh bhi easy hai. Ab baar baar same cheez poochh rahi hai, boring lag raha hai.
child.sent: Hmm... pehle hum compass ko... wooden table pe rakhenge, kyunki steel table needle ko disturb karta hai. Phir... wait karenge needle settle hone tak... needle north dikhayegi... phir right side... east wall hogi. Bas, thak gayi, aur nahi karna!

turns.teacher: Theek hai, Mahi. Tumne correct steps use kiye: wooden surface, needle settle, then north se east. Aaj ka lesson yahin stop. Goodbye, Mahi—achchha rest karo.

end.summary:
Mahi practised how a freely suspended magnet settles north–south.
They stated that the magnet’s north pole points north across four unaided responses.
They practised using a compass to identify east and west from a facing direction.
They identified that steel can disturb a compass and that a wooden table is suitable.
Teach-back was not passed; compass-direction use remained unsettled.
end.parentNote: Asha practised magnet direction, compass use, and choosing a suitable surface for the compass. Mahi consistently used the north–south settling idea and explained that steel can disturb the needle. There was a mix-up about which side is east or west when facing south; it was corrected later when facing north, but the full compass method was not yet secure. At home, place a compass on a wooden table and practise naming the right and left directions while facing north, south, east, and west.
